surface_mechanism_description: The self-limited growth of InAs is achieved by alternating exposure of the substrate to TMIn and AsH3, with the residual precursors and boundary layer removed by mechanical shear-off. The prevention of precursor carryover and gas-phase decomposition ensures self-limited growth.
evidence: To achieve a self-limited growth, it is extremely important to accomplish an abrupt transition of group III and group V precursors and minimize gas-phase decompositions of the precursors, especially group III precursors. If, after the exposure of the substrate to one group precursor flux, there remain residual precursors and/or their products, those residues will react with the precursor of the other group element, which is supplied subsequently. Those reactions will cause an MOVPE-like growth, and no saturation of the growth rate will occur. In the gas-switching system, the residual reactants near the substrate disappear mainly by diffusion due to the concentration gradient, and mixing of the one group precursors with the other group precursors may occur. In addition, the prevention of the gas-phase decomposition is not complete, either. In a gas-switching system, it is not easy to remove the boundary layer that forms near the substrate. TMIn is reported to decompose at ~270 °C. There will be a high concentration of decomposed products of TMIn in the gas phase above 370 °C if the boundary layer is not purged out completely. These decomposed TMIn products cause multilayer adsorption of indium species, resulting in a nonsaturated growth.
